decisions.title: Use Overture Maps Places as the primary free discovery source
decisions.context: Production requires scalable free US/Canada business discovery without paid APIs/public-community Overpass dependence.
decisions.decision: Use Overture Maps Places resolved through its STAC catalog as primary production discovery.
consequences: No paid discovery dependency.
Quality depends on source/provider coverage.
Bounded public-site enrichment remains needed for missing phones.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Public source data only.
Free-source model preserved.
Source timeouts/partitions are bounded.
decisions.reversibility: Reversible through source adapter after evidence-backed replacement.
decisions.decided_by: legacy project decision reconstructed from repository evidence

decisions.title: Use Cloudflare R2 hashed fingerprints as permanent cross-day dedupe authority
decisions.context: Daily lead history grows indefinitely and raw contact fields are unnecessary for duplicate blocking.
decisions.decision: Use type-separated 96-bit BLAKE2 tokens in packed-v2 R2 shards with historical objects-v1 read compatibility and pending recovery.
consequences: Scalable duplicate history without raw lead storage in R2.
Fingerprint history should not be expired merely for space.
Pack/pending writes require locking/recovery discipline.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: R2 stores hashed fingerprints.
Cloudflare credentials are server-only.
Object storage avoids a bounded SQL tier.
decisions.reversibility: Migratable with registry audit/backfill; deleting history without migration weakens dedupe.
decisions.decided_by: legacy project decision reconstructed from repository evidence

decisions.title: Keep full accepted lead records in dated Google Sheets
decisions.context: Operators need daily consumable workbooks while R2 only needs dedupe state.
decisions.decision: Write full records to one dated Google workbook; use R2 only for permanent fingerprints/telemetry.
consequences: Daily workbooks are directly usable.
Workbook readiness/ownership is a production dependency.
R2 cannot reconstruct full records.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Google credentials stay secret.
Dated files bound operational scope.
No raw production copy to lower environments without approval.
decisions.reversibility: Storage adapter can change through approved migration/parity verification.
decisions.decided_by: legacy project decision reconstructed from repository evidence

decisions.title: Use GitHub Actions plus serialized recovery supervisor as production controller
decisions.context: Project needs a zero-server scheduled controller with bounded retries and no competing recovery runs.
decisions.decision: Run on GitHub-hosted Actions with serialized concurrency, recovery supervisor, timeouts, midnight guards and health evidence.
consequences: No paid always-on server.
GitHub Actions is an operational dependency.
Late catch-up stops when safe runway is insufficient.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: PR validation has no production credentials.
Secrets injected only into real-run steps.
Hosted-runner constraints shape budgets.
decisions.reversibility: Can move schedulers if equivalent concurrency, identity, secret and evidence controls are retained.
decisions.decided_by: legacy project decision reconstructed from repository evidence

decisions.title: Adopt ANPOS as governance overlay without resetting existing product
decisions.context: Lead Engine already had production history P01-P70 before ANPOS 1.4.0.
decisions.decision: Preserve existing implementation/history and use ANPOS for governance, traceability and future work.
consequences: Legacy checkpoints remain evidence.
Project lifecycle is production_operations.
Future control-plane work follows protected checks.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Vendor-only ANPOS runtime excluded.
No AI identity fabricated.
Governance changes remain protected.
decisions.reversibility: ANPOS can evolve through versioned migration; completed repo evidence cannot be silently discarded.
decisions.decided_by: VSN repository owner instruction plus verified adoption

decisions.title: Treat multi-platform lead SaaS as a new product direction while preserving the existing production engine
decisions.context: User requested subscription web/desktop/mobile experiences, configurable sources and scheduled user jobs in the existing ANPOS-enabled VSN Lead Engine repository. The repository already runs a production daily lead workflow.
alternatives: Plan SaaS as an additive product direction and preserve production operations
Move implementation into a dedicated SaaS repository before code work
decisions.decision: Keep SaaS planning and implementation additive in the current repository while isolating the existing production lead runtime. The AI may later split a dedicated application repository only if architecture/operational evidence shows a clear benefit; that technical move does not require per-step owner confirmation when reversible and zero-new-spend.
consequences: System design and safe implementation can proceed without a repository-boundary confirmation pause.
Existing production lead flow remains isolated and protected by its current invariants.
A later repository split must preserve history, CI, security and traceability.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Avoids accidental disruption to production lead flow.
Future SaaS requires tenant isolation, provider rights, cost caps and new privacy/retention controls.
decisions.reversibility: Reversible before code implementation; moving plans/source to a dedicated repo requires traceability migration.
decisions.decided_by: VSN repository owner standing technical delegation plus ANPOS evidence-backed selection

decisions.title: Propose an evidence-gated, web-first SaaS MVP
decisions.context: User requested a multi-platform lead SaaS with subscriptions, scheduled country/niche searches, free/paid/custom source options, admin, AI and rich landing site. The repository's production lead engine is an existing Python CLI/workflow and no customer interviews, approved launch market, provider distribution rights, unit economics, stack or repo boundary have been decided.
alternatives: Build all web/desktop/mobile surfaces and broad integrations together
Start with responsive web after validating one target segment and one permitted source path
Implement SaaS in this production repo immediately
Create a dedicated SaaS application repo before product code
decisions.decision: Adopt a reversible development baseline: responsive web first on shared versioned APIs; preserve US+Canada compatibility as the initial engineering scope; keep source integration policy-aware and provider-disabled until rights are established; default to free/zero-new-paid-spend development paths and allow BYOK-capable interfaces without activating paid providers; defer native desktop/mobile until the API/web contracts stabilize. This authorizes development sequencing, not a claim of customer demand, legal clearance, provider rights, pricing approval or public launch readiness.
consequences: System/data/threat/UX design can proceed immediately without owner technical confirmation.
Customer research remains evidence for product validation but is no longer a blocker to reversible architecture and implementation work.
Paid providers, commercial billing activation and public launch remain separately gated.
Desktop/mobile remain later clients against stable shared APIs.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Tenant isolation and least privilege are P0 architecture gates.
Source/field/country rights and retention must be checked before activation.
Paid and AI operations require estimates, explicit opt-in, per-tenant hard caps and kill switches.
Current production operations must remain isolated and unchanged.
Hosted CI runner use follows the repository runner-minimization policy without skipping required checks.
decisions.reversibility: Planning proposal is reversible until accepted. If accepted, changes require a superseding ADR with evidence and migration/compatibility impact.
decisions.decided_by: VSN repository owner standing technical delegation plus ANPOS evidence-backed recommendation

decisions.title: Use Next.js for the additive SaaS frontend and retain Django authority
decisions.context: Owner requested Next frontend and milestone-sequenced continuation on the existing Django/DRF SaaS foundation.
alternatives: Retain Django templates for all UI
Next.js App Router/TypeScript with Django API
decisions.decision: Select Next.js App Router and TypeScript under apps/web; partially supersede only the earlier stack ADR Web UI selection. Django/DRF/PostgreSQL/session authority and production collector isolation remain.
consequences: Adds a pinned Node build/runtime and npm dependency review.
Preserved Django forms allow incremental UI migration.
Frontend does not certify source rights, billing or release acceptance.
security_privacy_data_operational_cost_i: Server-only session GET transport; Django checks membership; no shared customer cache or public proxy.
CSRF mutations stay on tested Django forms.
No paid service or deployment activated.
decisions.reversibility: Route UI back to preserved Django pages without changing backend or collector data.
decisions.decided_by: Owner Next.js preference and standing technical implementation delegation

rules: Accepted material decisions must not be silently reversed.
A replacement decision must preserve supersession traceability.
Decision evidence must distinguish verified facts from inference.
